name: Propantheline

lead: Propantheline is an older tablet that dermatology references list for excessive sweating, and people who want to stay dry and presentable look to it for that purpose.

It blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors, reducing gland secretion and smooth muscle contraction. References group it with glycopyrrolate and oxybutynin as oral anticholinergics for focal and generalised hyperhidrosis, and it is also used for stomach and bladder spasm. No clinical trial of propantheline for sweating was identified; the literature concerns mainly bladder and gastric use.

paras: It is taken as a tablet under medical direction. Less sweating is the expected effect, alongside general gland drying.
Fast heart rate, constipation, light sensitivity, dry mouth, blurred vision and urinary retention are reported. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Propantheline is an older anticholinergic tablet that dermatology references list for excessive sweating, used by people who want drier skin and clothes. It blocks the signal that makes sweat glands secrete. Information on its sweat use comes mainly from reference listings rather than sweat trials.

lead: Propantheline bromide is an oral antimuscarinic drug that blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in smooth muscle, glands and the eye. Reference works list it for excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis), cramps or spasms of the stomach, intestines or bladder, and involuntary urination; dentists sometimes use it to reduce salivation. A brand name is Pro-Banthine [1].

Dermatology references group it with glycopyrrolate and oxybutynin as oral anticholinergics used for focal and generalised hyperhidrosis [2]. The published literature found for this entry concerns mainly bladder and gastric uses; no clinical trial of propantheline for sweating was identified.
infobox: Hyperhidrosis, GI and bladder spasm, enuresis [1]

paras: By blocking muscarinic receptors it reduces secretions including sweat and tears [1]. Common side effects listed are fast heart rate, constipation, light sensitivity, dry mouth and urinary retention [1][2].

A randomised double-blind trial compared oxybutynin, propantheline and placebo for detrusor hyperactivity [3], and a Cochrane review examined anticholinergics for overactive bladder [4]. Pharmacology studies used propantheline to slow gastric emptying in healthy volunteers [5]. No study found tested propantheline for sweating as an appearance concern.
